title: The life gas ledger
description: What each life class puts into the air and takes out of it, and how much (GEN.891, GEN.857, GEN.858, GEN.859; docs/design/habitability/life-classes.md sections 4 and 6; research: reports/non-oxygen-life-byproducts-2026-10-28.md). Rows are keyed by life class number. Every number carries its source tier (T1 to T9) and tweak level (L0 to L4) next to it. The methane flux of a class is its fuel supply (a share of Earth's, physics/life_supply.py) times the area over Earth's times the flux Earth's supply would give; the air holds the flux times the methane's lifetime, up to a cap, and the carbon comes from the air's own carbon dioxide. Every class variant also lists its balanced reactions under `reactions` (GEN.1743; research reports/ledger-rates-gen1742-2026-11-15.md): what it takes and gives off, the energy it runs on, what limits its flux and whether it changes the air; a reaction must balance every element and the charge (species are written with their charge after a caret, `SO4^2-`).

earth_donor_methane_tmol_yr.basis: The methane, Tmol a year, that the anoxygenic communities of an Earth-sized world give when its donor supply is Earth's: photoferrotrophs on 80 Tmol of Fe2+ a year fix 20 Tmol of carbon and the food web returns 0.5 methane per carbon, 10 Tmol ([R3393], read; 0.37e11 molecules/cm2/s), inside the 9 to 67 Tmol of [R2336] (read)

earth_h2_tmol_yr.basis: The hydrogen, Tmol a year, an Earth-sized world's hydrogenotrophs have when its hydrogen supply is Earth's: Earth's outgassing of 1.7 to 2.9 Tmol a year ([R3393], read); four hydrogen make one methane, so the methane is a quarter of it

h2_per_methane.basis: CO2 + 4 H2 -> CH4 + 2 H2O (the stoichiometry of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis)

methane_per_buried_carbon.basis: 2 CH2O -> CH4 + CO2: the organic carbon that is buried or fermented with no oxidant left ends half as methane (stoichiometry)

methane_lifetime_yr.basis: The life of methane in an air with no free oxygen, years: [R2336] give 100 ppmv to 3.5 percent of methane for 9 to 67 Tmol a year, which is 2e3 to 9e4 years, and [R0693] (read) call it long-lived where hydroxyl is scarce; the geometric middle

methane_max_share.basis: The most methane of an anoxic air, as a share of its molecules: 3.5 percent ([R2336], read abstract)

carbon_left_share.basis: The share of the air's carbon dioxide that methane-making life leaves in the air: the methane's carbon comes out of it, so it cannot take more than it has

oxygen_max_share.basis: The most free oxygen, as a share of the air's molecules, in which methane builds up: above a part in a thousand hydroxyl and ozone chemistry give methane a life of decades (Earth's, 21 percent oxygen, holds 1.8 ppmv); the methane of a ledger row is not added to an air with more oxygen than this

hydrogen_max_share.basis: The most hydrogen an air holds where hydrogen-eating life lives, as a mole share: at or below 1e-4 ([R0693], read; [R2336])

apply_rise.basis: The air takes new methane only when the target is this much above what it holds, so that applying the ledger again changes nothing (a numerical choice)

h2s_max_share.basis: The most hydrogen sulfide an air holds where sulfur-eating life lives, as a mole share (GEN.894): Earth's modern air holds tens of parts per trillion (recalled) and a volcanic reduced air much more where nothing eats it; one part in a hundred million is the cap the ledger gives a world with sulfur eaters or acid eaters. A design floor, no source gives a sulfur-eater limit

sulfur_dioxide_per_h2s.basis: The acid eaters of Classes 5 and 9 oxidise the hydrogen sulfide they take to sulfur dioxide: sulfur is conserved, one mole of SO2 for each mole of H2S (the oxygen comes from the acid; stoichiometry)

methane_per_h2_hydrogenated.basis: C2H2 + 3 H2 -> 2 CH4: the cold hydrogenators of Class 7 make two methane from the three hydrogen they take (stoichiometry); the carbon comes from the haze acetylene, not from the air's gases, which the air does not store

earth_nitrogen_fixed_tmol_yr.basis: Earth's natural nitrogen fixation, Tmol N a year: about 220 Tg N (100 on land, 120 in the sea, Galloway as summarised in Steffen et al., read second-hand) over 14 g/mol (reports/ledger-rates-gen1742-2026-11-15.md section 2.1)

n2o_per_nitrogen_fixed.basis: The nitrous oxide nitrogen that leaks from nitrifiers and denitrifiers per nitrogen fixed: natural N2O 17.0 Tg N a year less 7.3 from people ([R5287], read) over about 220 Tg N fixed; two read numbers carried to other worlds by inference (GEN.1742 section 2.4)

n2o_lifetime_yr.basis: The life of nitrous oxide in the air, years (IPCC AR6, recalled; photolysis sets it with or without oxygen)

oxic_methane_lifetime_yr.basis: The life of methane in an oxygenated air, years: IPCC TAR WG1 Table 4.2 note (read), 1,745 ppb, 2.78 Tg/ppb and a loss of 576 Tg a year

soil_methane_sink_share.basis: The share of an oxygenated air's methane loss that soil methane eaters take: 30 of 576 Tg a year (IPCC TAR WG1 Table 4.2, read); the rest is hydroxyl (506) and the stratosphere (40)

seafloor_methane_eaten_share.basis: The share of the methane made under the seafloor that methane eaters take before it reaches the water above, once the sea holds sulfate: more than 90 percent ([R5286], read); the sea gives under 2 percent of the world's methane to the air

co_deposition_life_cm_s.basis: The deposition velocity of carbon monoxide into a sea with CO-eating life, cm/s ([R2336] as quoted and used in [R4729], read)

co_deposition_abiotic_cm_s.basis: The deposition velocity of carbon monoxide into a sea with no CO-eating life, cm/s ([R2336] as quoted in [R4729], read)

1.name: Oxygenic light-eaters
1.note: Before the oxygen rise the food web of the buried organic carbon makes methane and carbon dioxide; at the rise the oxygen burns the methane (physics/biogenic_oxygen.py), so the row gives none after it. Oxygen itself is GEN.855.
1.basis: The byproducts report's table (an anoxic air with oxygenic photosynthesis holds methane until the reductants are spent) and life-classes.md section 4, row 1

2.name: Anoxygenic light-eaters
2.note: Carbon is fixed with H2, Fe2+ or H2S for electrons; the food web makes the methane, donor-limited at 1e-4 to 1e-2 of today's biosphere. Never any oxygen.
2.basis: The byproducts report section 4 [R0693, R2336, R3393]

3.name: Hydrogen eaters
3.note: A methane source on a world with open hydrogen (small); sealed sub-ice and aquifer worlds show nothing in the air because the supply is the water's contact with the rock. 3b (sulfate) makes sulfide, not methane, and is not modelled: its row gives none.
3.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 3; the stoichiometry of hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis

4.name: Chemolithotrophs
4.note: Draws hydrogen sulfide down to a part in a hundred million and makes sulfate in the water (not an air gas); the air effect is the missing H2S. The size is capped by how fast the oxidant arrives, which the class's supply terms already do.
4.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 4; the H2S cap is a design floor (h2s_max_share)

5.name: Acid eaters
5.note: Acid eaters take reduced sulfur (hydrogen sulfide) and put sulfur dioxide into the air, so the air shifts from H2S to SO2 in the same moles. The elemental sulfur, carbon dioxide, and water they also give off are not air changes the ledger tracks. The sulfur dioxide share is the acid medium's own supply (GEN.888).
5.basis: life-classes.md section 4, rows 5 and 9: speculative chemistry; the climates report's own bookkeeping, no source gives rates

6.name: Dense-carbon-dioxide hydrogen eaters
6.note: As Class 3, in a supercritical carbon dioxide fluid.
6.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 6 (a methane source; the water separates from the fluid)

7.name: Cold methane hydrogenators
7.note: Hydrogen goes down to its cap and methane up by two thirds of a mole for each mole of hydrogen taken. Acetylene goes down too, but the air does not store it, so that part is only in the text: the Titan hydrogen and acetylene anomalies are a lead, not a detection.
7.basis: life-classes.md section 4, row 7: the Titan anomalies are a lead, not a detection

8.name: Ammonia-water hydrogen eaters
8.note: As Class 3 (the net air effect is small).

9.name: Silicon acid eaters
9.note: As Class 5, with silica deposits (a solid, not an air gas).
9.basis: life-classes.md section 4, rows 5 and 9: speculative chemistry

oxygenic_photosynthesis.name: Oxygenic photosynthesis
oxygenic_photosynthesis.basis: Water split by light, carbon dioxide made into organic carbon; only the carbon buried leaves oxygen and takes carbon dioxide from the air for good (physics/biogenic_oxygen.py, GEN.855); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

aerobic_respiration.name: Aerobic respiration
aerobic_respiration.basis: The eaters of the producers' carbon return what the producers made; the net of the two is the burial, so the air sees only the burial row; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

food_web_methane.name: Fermentation to methane
food_web_methane.basis: 2 CH2O -> CH4 + CO2: organic carbon fermented with no oxidant left ends half as methane (`methane_per_buried_carbon`); the classes' methane rows give the flux; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

nitrogen_fixation.name: Nitrogen fixation
nitrogen_fixation.basis: Nitrogenase, with the electrons of organic carbon; Earth's natural fixation about 220 Tg N a year (`earth_nitrogen_fixed_tmol_yr`); denitrification returns it, so the nitrogen of the air changes only by the organic nitrogen buried (reports/ledger-rates-gen1742-2026-11-15.md section 2.1); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

photoferrotrophy.name: Iron-using anoxygenic photosynthesis
photoferrotrophy.basis: 4 Fe2+ + CO2 + 11 H2O -> CH2O + 4 Fe(OH)3 + 8 H+ ([R3393], read); the donor supply is Earth's 80 Tmol of Fe2+ a year [R3393]. The Fe(III) buried is oxidant that is not oxygen; its buried share has no source yet, so the air history does not use it (GEN.1742 section 2.2)

sulfide_to_sulfur.name: Sulfide-using anoxygenic photosynthesis (to sulfur)
sulfide_to_sulfur.basis: Green and purple sulfur bacteria; draws the air's hydrogen sulfide to its cap (`h2s_max_share`); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

sulfide_to_sulfate.name: Sulfide-using anoxygenic photosynthesis (to sulfate)
sulfide_to_sulfate.basis: The same eaters taking the sulfide on to sulfate; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

hydrogen_photosynthesis.name: Hydrogen-using anoxygenic photosynthesis
hydrogen_photosynthesis.basis: Draws the air's hydrogen to its cap (`hydrogen_max_share`, [R0693]); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

hydrogenotrophic_methanogenesis.name: Methane from hydrogen
hydrogenotrophic_methanogenesis.basis: Methanogens run to about 30 kJ/mol and turn more than 95 percent of the hydrogen that reaches them into methane ([R4729], read); Earth's hydrogen supply 2.3 Tmol a year (`earth_h2_tmol_yr`); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

hydrogen_acetogenesis.name: Acetate from hydrogen
hydrogen_acetogenesis.basis: Acetogens share the hydrogen supply with the methanogens; the acetate is split to methane (acetoclastic_methanogenesis), so the net is the methane row's; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

acetoclastic_methanogenesis.name: Methane from acetate
acetoclastic_methanogenesis.basis: Acetate splitters; inside the methane rows' flux; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

carbon_monoxide_acetogenesis.name: Acetate from carbon monoxide
carbon_monoxide_acetogenesis.basis: CO eaters are the main carbon monoxide sink of an anoxic air: a deposition velocity of 1.2e-4 cm/s into a sea with them against 1e-8 cm/s without ([R2336] as quoted in [R4729], read); the acetate goes on to methane (GEN.1742 section 2.3)

hydrogenotrophic_sulfate_reduction.name: Sulfide from sulfate and hydrogen
hydrogenotrophic_sulfate_reduction.basis: Sulfate reducers on radiolytic hydrogen; the sulfate is the sea's (little in an anoxic sea), the hydrogen sulfide is held under `h2s_max_share`; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

anaerobic_methane_oxidation.name: Methane eaten with sulfate
anaerobic_methane_oxidation.basis: Archaea with sulfate reducers eat more than 90 percent of the methane made under the seafloor once the sea holds sulfate ([R5286], read; `seafloor_methane_eaten_share`); the sink that helped end the Archean methane air [R5250]; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

aerobic_sulfide_oxidation.name: Sulfide eaten with oxygen
aerobic_sulfide_oxidation.basis: Draws hydrogen sulfide to `h2s_max_share`; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

aerobic_iron_oxidation.name: Iron eaten with oxygen
aerobic_iron_oxidation.basis: Uses oxygen the producers made; inside the oxygen law's reductant sink (physics/biogenic_oxygen.py); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

nitrification.name: Ammonium eaten with oxygen
nitrification.basis: Ammonium to nitrate; the nitrate is the oxidant of 4b; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

nitrification_nitrous_oxide.name: Nitrous oxide from nitrification
nitrification_nitrous_oxide.basis: The leak of nitrifiers and denitrifiers together: 0.044 of the nitrogen fixed leaves as N2O (natural 9.7 Tg N a year of about 220 fixed, GEN.1742 section 2.4); lives `n2o_lifetime_yr` in the air

aerobic_methane_oxidation.name: Methane eaten with oxygen
aerobic_methane_oxidation.basis: Soil methane eaters take 30 of the 576 Tg a year an oxygenated air loses (IPCC TAR WG1 Table 4.2, read; `soil_methane_sink_share`); the rest is the air's chemistry, a life of 8.4 years (`oxic_methane_lifetime_yr`); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

denitrification.name: Organic carbon eaten with nitrate
denitrification.basis: Returns the nitrogen fixed to the air; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

denitrification_nitrous_oxide.name: Nitrous oxide from denitrification
denitrification_nitrous_oxide.basis: As nitrification_nitrous_oxide: the two leaks share one yield

nitrate_sulfide_oxidation.name: Sulfide eaten with nitrate
nitrate_sulfide_oxidation.basis: Draws hydrogen sulfide to `h2s_max_share`; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

nitrate_iron_oxidation.name: Iron eaten with nitrate
nitrate_iron_oxidation.basis: stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

nitrate_ammonium_oxidation.name: Ammonium eaten with nitrate
nitrate_ammonium_oxidation.basis: stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

nitrate_methane_oxidation.name: Methane eaten with nitrate
nitrate_methane_oxidation.basis: stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

perchlorate_sulfide_oxidation.name: Sulfide eaten with perchlorate
perchlorate_sulfide_oxidation.basis: Draws hydrogen sulfide to `h2s_max_share`; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

perchlorate_iron_oxidation.name: Iron eaten with perchlorate
perchlorate_iron_oxidation.basis: stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

perchlorate_ammonium_oxidation.name: Ammonium eaten with perchlorate
perchlorate_ammonium_oxidation.basis: stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

perchlorate_methane_oxidation.name: Methane eaten with perchlorate
perchlorate_methane_oxidation.basis: stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

chlorite_dismutation.name: Oxygen from chlorite
chlorite_dismutation.basis: The perchlorate eaters' own oxygen, used again inside the cell: none reaches the air (GEN.1742 section 2.4); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

acid_sulfide_oxidation.name: Sulfide eaten with sulfuric acid
acid_sulfide_oxidation.basis: The acid's own sulfur came from the air's sulfur dioxide, so over the cycle the air gains one SO2 for each H2S (`sulfur_dioxide_per_h2s`); speculative chemistry, the reaction itself balanced

acid_sulfur_comproportionation.name: Sulfur from sulfide and sulfuric acid
acid_sulfur_comproportionation.basis: The elemental sulfur the acid eaters leave; speculative chemistry, the reaction itself balanced

acid_carbon_oxidation.name: Organic carbon eaten with sulfuric acid
acid_carbon_oxidation.basis: The acid eaters' food; a cycle with the acid's remaking; speculative chemistry, the reaction itself balanced

acetylene_hydrogenation.name: Methane from acetylene
acetylene_hydrogenation.basis: The Titan hydrogen and acetylene anomalies are a lead, not a detection; the acetylene is not an air gas the air stores (`methane_per_h2_hydrogenated`); stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio

anaerobic_ammonium_oxidation.name: Nitrogen from ammonium and nitrite
anaerobic_ammonium_oxidation.basis: Anammox; the nitrite of a cold ammonia-water world is a guess (lightning and photochemistry), so the air history takes no flux from it until the ammonia cap of GEN.1732 is decided; stoichiometry: the balanced equation fixes every ratio
